## Summary (human-written)
<!-- Write this yourself, not with an AI tool. 2-5 sentences: the problem, why
     this approach, and what you checked yourself. -->

## Rebase and review status

Current head: `7b33941e84099436504bbd893ac13ac6a2e3e261`. The stack is rebased onto fetched upstream main
`73c4ebdac57de0d89bb20d5dfabed340449c8b0d`; commit prefixes now match the four PR titles.
The latest `pr-review` skill and checklist were read from this rebased checkout.

The rebase updates the `PrecisionConfig` parallelize contract, checks QSA
accelerator capture before dynamic metadata construction, preserves Flash-Next's
BF16 GDN parameter policy, restores the PP test imports, and retains upstream's
redundant-test deletions. Current exact-prefix checks: all-file pre-commit passes
and 77 CPU tests pass. The full-stack CPU run hides GPUs so the
upstream CPU FSDP test does not select the unavailable FA4 package.

[Claude's review of #5782](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5782#pullrequestreview-5761648327)
still has open FSDP/indexer and QSA training-memory findings. Earlier local
approval claims are withdrawn. HF/GPU/convergence results below are historical
captures at their stated SHAs; this rebase has not received fresh GPU validation.
The human summary placeholder is retained for the author to complete before review.

## Why

The preceding model increment rejects PP. Flash-Next carries four residual
streams, and PLE needs original token IDs and document positions even when its
layer is on a later stage. The final stream mixer must remain with the language
model head. This PR uses the existing pipeline hooks to preserve those contracts
and supplies combined training and a repeatable numerical regression fixture.

**Example.** Four virtual stages over PP2:

```text
stage 0: token embedding + layer 0 -> [T, 4D]
stage 1: layers 1-3, including PLE -> [T, 4D]
stage 2: layers 4-5                -> [T, 4D]
stage 3: layers 6-7 + stream mixer + language-model head
original token IDs and document positions reach every stage
four microbatches use Interleaved1F1B with full activation remat
```

## What changed

- Enable real PP through the inherited `BaseModel.pipeline` hooks and pin the
  stream mixer with `pipeline_last_stage_module_fqns`. Fake PP raises because
  its static metadata assumes one residual stream.
- Add a packed-document CPU split-model forward/backward check for the original
  ID payload, PLE after a stage boundary, and every stage parameter gradient.
- Register the real eight-GPU FSDP2/TP2/EP4/PP2 recipe in the model and H100 suites:
  four virtual stages, four microbatches, Interleaved1F1B and full remat.
- Register a GB300 TP2/EP2/SP numerical fixture with its exported loss/grad_norm
  golden and public hardware/software/source/data provenance.
- Mechanical: move the existing TP2 recipe beside the new PP recipes and extend
  the existing suite-registration checks.

The shared engine rejects SPMD typechecking under PP. The combined PP recipe
uses that supported contract; the TP2/EP2/SP numerical fixture checks types.
This PR depends on `[qwen3_8_fn] 3/n`.

## User-facing changes

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Flash-Next rejects pipeline parallelism | PP2 forwards four streams and the original-ID/document-position payload through the existing stage hooks |
| No combined Flash-Next integration recipe | Real FSDP2/TP2/EP4/PP2 training with four virtual stages and full remat |
| No GB300 numerical regression | `--test_suite gb300 --gpu_arch gb300` selects the committed TP2/EP2/SP loss/grad_norm fixture |

## Numerics

The historical qualified golden-bearing head is `48795a820e3016848b5061aadb55a21aa06a28dc`,
based on upstream `a87db08ea73cbdd567ceb055bd9118fd4a4507b2`. The qualified
pre-golden source is `07d0138e3203ec872fa54f39e3cd2b135a5584ac`; it is archived
[here](https://github.com/shuhuayu/torchtitan/commit/07d0138e3203ec872fa54f39e3cd2b135a5584ac).
Only the exported golden, provenance and README were added after qualification.
That statement compares the historical qualification and golden-bearing refs;
it does not establish numerical equivalence of the current rebase.

| Check | Hardware/layout | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Full/split CPU model | Packed documents; PLE after boundary | Exact forward; every stage parameter gradient passes FP32 bounds |
| PP2 versus unsplit offline | Two GB300; fixed checkpoint/batch; all 190 gradients | Original bounds pass; norm ratio 0.999999925571, cosine 0.999999402373 |
| PP2 plain/full remat | Two GB300; seed 42, strict deterministic; ten steps | All 20 full-precision loss/grad_norm values are bitwise equal |
| Upstream rebase regression | Two GB300; PP2/full remat; same FP32 seed checkpoint | All 20 values match the historical source bitwise |
| Independent remote repeats | GB300; TP2/EP2/SP; ten steps in each independent launch | All 20 values agree bitwise |
| Registered export | GB300; public integration runner | Exported text agrees bitwise with both independent launches |
| Registered replay from committed head | GB300; public integration runner without export | All 20 values agree bitwise at `48795a8`; imported loss and grad_norm assertions pass |
| Combined offline and training | Eight GB300 across two hosts; FSDP2/TP2/EP4/PP2 | All 190 gradients and natural choices pass; ten optimizer steps complete |

The historical local PP2/remat captures above use `cb0444dea14eb5a351e978866bf01872022f157f`.
The earlier rebased PP2/full-remat regression and remote GB300 captures use
`07d0138e`. The shared deterministic backward policy is supplied by the preceding
PR; this increment changes no non-PP forward equation.

The eight-rank run reconstructs every preclip gradient with unchanged BF16
RMS/infinity bounds (`atol=1e-4`, `rtol=0.03125`), without fitted rescaling:
global norm ratio 1.0001680912226776, cosine 0.9999607227562836.
All 570 replicated gradient copies, 80 routing records and 176 replicated/remat
choices pass. Source hashes and dependency versions match on all eight ranks.
Ten optimizer steps reduce loss from 7.800787925720215 to 5.32912540435791.

The offline matrix uses the separately disclosed forward-conditioned PLE
fixture: key feature-zero gain 0.125, selected before observing distributed
gradients, requiring raw key/query dot >= 1 and sigmoid(signed sqrt) <= 0.9.
The actual eight-rank minimum/maximum are 1.0390625 / 0.875. Reference, C4,
public training recipe and golden initialization remain unmodified. The original
near-zero SP peak-bound outlier is retained and documented in the prior PR.

Historical full-stack captures also establish pinned HF text/image/video
forward/backward parity and 100-step C4 convergence at their recorded sources. These historical captures keep their source
attributions in the preceding PR descriptions.

## GB300 golden

`tests/assets/losses/real_pg/gb300/qwen3_8_flash_next.txt` is the actual registered
runner export, SHA256 `9314e9e77420783e8dfddbae7ef6748bca1ffc723b235e371324d8904813bb57`.
Its neighboring provenance JSON records the pinned source, dependencies, data,
init/parameter/reduce dtypes, optimizer, schedule and supported layout.
Each qualification launch independently creates the stock model-only FP32
seed checkpoint. The fixture uses seed 42, strict determinism, ten steps,
TP2/EP2/SP, no remat, no local compile regions and real process groups.
Two training GPUs are used on a four-GPU GB300 host. Loss goes from
7.638507843017578 to 6.054037094116211; no conditioned offline weights are used.

```bash
python -m tests.integration_tests.run_tests outputs/qwen38-gb300 \
  --test_suite gb300 --execution_mode real_pg --gpu_arch gb300 --ngpu 2 \
  --test_name qwen3_8_flash_next_tp+ep_numerics
```

## Testing and CI selection

- All-file pre-commit hooks pass, including the committed golden/provenance.
- 77 focused CPU model/config/integration-definition/FSDP cases pass. The split
  regression checks original IDs, packed boundaries and all stage gradients.
- Verified the actual combined recipe is selected in the eight-GPU model
  real-PG job, including `real_pg_required`, and excluded from fake PG.
  H100 selection uses the same recipe; the remote execution ran on GB300.
- GB300 is a dedicated remote hardware suite. The current OSS workflow has no
  GB300 runner; its registered path resolves to the committed GB300 asset.
- The historical registered replay from `48795a8` passed all 20 bitwise
  metric checks. It has not been repeated for this rebase. The earlier local
  approval claim is withdrawn while parent #5782's findings remain open.

```bash
NGPU=8 MODULE=torchtitan_recipes.tests.models.qwen3_8_flash_next \
  CONFIG=qwen38_flash_next_debugmodel_all_parallelism ./run_train.sh
pre-commit run --all-files
```

## Alternatives considered

- A model-specific pipeline engine would duplicate existing stage ownership
  and schedule machinery.
- Putting PLE only on stage 0 would leave its later-stage original-ID contract
  unexercised; the four-stage recipe places it on stage 1.
- A single local numerical capture does not establish independent remote
  repeatability; qualification and export use remote GB300 launches.

Full-size lexical conversion/training, sparse-attention throughput/memory and CP
remain outside the verified scope. No performance improvement is claimed.

## Stack

This stack supersedes [the earlier all-in-one draft #5655](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5655).
Its original branch and worktree are retained for reference.

Draft 4/n of the Flash-Next implementation.

- [1/n Add Flash-Next model, FSDP and checkpoint reference coverage](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5782)
- [2/n Add tensor and expert parallelism with batched QSA teachers](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5783)
- [3/n Honor deterministic GDN normalization](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5784)
- [4/n Add pipeline stages, remat and numerical integration coverage](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5785)

Depends on [3/n](https://github.com/pytorch/torchtitan/pull/5784).
Its review base is `users/shuhuayu/qwen3-8-fn-04-determinism`. After the parent lands,
rebase as needed and retarget this PR to `main` before merging.
